member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Barcodes.Code128Encoder
member.summary: Encodes a string as a Code 128 (1-D) barcode and returns the bar/space module pattern: a flat array of equal-width modules where true is a bar (dark) and false is a space (light). The pattern includes the Start B symbol, the modulo-103 symbol check, the Stop symbol and its terminating bar; the caller applies the bar width (X-dimension) and quiet zone when laying it into a box.
member.remarks: Code Set B is used throughout — it covers all printable ASCII (32..126), which is what Altium stores for a silkscreen ID barcode — so any single-byte text round-trips to the same decoded value regardless of the code-set optimisation a generator might otherwise choose.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Barcodes.Code128Encoder.TryEncode(System.String,System.Boolean[]@)
member.summary: Encodes as a Code 128 B module pattern. Returns false (with a null pattern) if the text is empty or contains a character outside printable ASCII (32..126).

member.summary: An encoded ECC200 Data Matrix symbol: a square (or rectangular) grid of light/dark modules. is indexed [row, col] with row 0 at the TOP of the symbol and true meaning a dark module. The grid does not include the surrounding quiet zone — that is the caller's responsibility when rendering.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Barcodes.DataMatrixEncoder
member.summary: Encoder for ISO/IEC 16022 ECC200 Data Matrix symbols. Converts a text string into a grid of dark/light modules using ASCII encodation, automatic (smallest-fitting) square symbol sizing, Reed-Solomon error correction over GF(256), and the standard Annex F module placement.
member.remarks:
This is the symbology Altium uses for a PCB Text primitive whose is . Altium stores only the source text (the module pattern is not persisted), so the renderer encodes the symbol on the fly.
Only ASCII encodation is implemented (digit pairs, single ASCII bytes, and an upper-shift escape for bytes 128-255). This always produces a valid, scannable symbol; it may occasionally pick a symbol one size larger than an encoder that also uses the C40/Text/Base256 schemes, but for typical part numbers, serial numbers and URLs the result is identical. Only square symbols are emitted (Altium's default).

member.summary: Encodes into an ECC200 Data Matrix symbol.
member.exception: is null.
is empty.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Barcodes.QrCodeEncoder
member.summary: Encoder for ISO/IEC 18004 QR Code symbols (model 2). Selects the smallest version that fits the data at the requested error-correction level, encodes using numeric / alphanumeric / byte mode, adds Reed-Solomon error correction, lays out the function and data modules, and applies the lowest-penalty data mask.
member.remarks: This is the symbology Altium uses for a PCB Text primitive whose is . The module pattern is not stored in the file, so the renderer encodes it on the fly. Kanji and ECI modes are not implemented (byte mode covers the remaining cases). Output is verified byte-identical to the segno reference QR library.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Connectivity.Internal.BusRange.RangeRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(?<prefix>.*?)\\[\\s*(?<from>\\d+)\\s*\\.\\.\\s*(?<to>\\d+)\\s*\\](?<suffix>.*)$
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ "prefix" capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' lazily any number of times.
○ Match '['.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ "from" capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ Match the string "..".
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ "to" capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ Match ']'.
○ "suffix" capture group.
○ Match a character other than '\n' greedily any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Connectivity.Internal.HarnessResolver
member.summary: Resolves harness-bundle connectivity. Inside each sheet a harness connector's bundle output is wired (through signal harnesses) to a harness port or a bundle net label that names the bundle (e.g. MEZIO). Each member entry of the connector is therefore a qualified net bundle.member (e.g. MEZIO.MEZ_SPI4_CS2); the same qualified member appears wherever the bundle is broken out, so unioning member entries by qualified name across the whole project reconnects harness signals.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Connectivity.NetIdentifierScope
member.summary: Altium's "Net Identifier Scope" project option. It decides whether net labels are sheet-local or global and how ports / sheet entries propagate connectivity across the hierarchy.
member.remarks: The setting lives in the [Design] section of the .PrjPcb file. Modern projects encode it with the HierarchyMode / NameNetsHierarchically flags; older projects use a spread of boolean flags (AllowPortNetNames, AllowSheetEntryNetNames, …). See .

member.name: F:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Connectivity.NetIdentifierScope.Automatic
member.summary: Altium picks the behaviour automatically: if the design has sheet entries / ports the scope is hierarchical; otherwise net labels and ports behave globally. This is the Altium default.

member.name: F:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Connectivity.NetIdentifierScope.Flat
member.summary: Flat: net labels are global across every sheet; ports are global too. Sheet symbols / sheet entries are ignored for connectivity. Suits single-tier flat multi-sheet designs.

member.name: F:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Connectivity.NetIdentifierScope.Hierarchical
member.summary: Hierarchical: net labels are local to their sheet; connectivity crosses sheet boundaries only through matching ports ↔ sheet entries. Power nets remain global by name.

member.name: F:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Connectivity.NetIdentifierScope.Global
member.summary: Global: net labels AND ports are global across the whole project, regardless of hierarchy.

member.summary: Unifies power objects / hidden power pins that share a name. Power on a non-repeated sheet is global by name. Power inside a repeated (multi-channel) instance is channel-private — keyed by the instance — so a channel-local rail (e.g. a per-channel 5V) does not merge with the same name in another channel or at board level; it escapes only through the port↔sheet-entry boundary, which carries a truly-global rail (e.g. GND) up to its global power object.
Unifies net labels and ports that share a name. Each is merged globally across all sheets or per-sheet depending on the active net-identifier scope.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbBoardOutline
member.summary:
Parses the board outline (physical board shape) from the Board6 parameter block.
Altium stores the outline as indexed vertices KIND{i}, VX{i}, VY{i}, CX{i}, CY{i}, SA{i}, EA{i}, R{i} forming a closed polygon, where KIND=0 is a straight segment to the next vertex and KIND=1 is a circular arc (centre CX/CY, radius R, start/end angle SA/EA). The final vertex repeats the first to close the loop.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbBoardOutline.Parse(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{System.String,System.String})
member.summary: Builds the board outline as a closed polygon of world-space points (arcs tessellated), or an empty list when the parameter block carries no outline.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbComponent.Children
member.summary: Every primitive this component owns, as a single de-duplicated sequence: pads, tracks, vias, arcs, text, fills, courtyard regions and 3D bodies — the typed primitives plus the shape-based regions/bodies (where modern boards keep footprint courtyards and 3D bodies).
member.remarks: This is a computed view, not stored state: it gathers the component's own child collections together with the document-level primitives linked back to it by ComponentIndex. A loaded PcbDoc keeps everything but pads in the document's flat lists, so this is the only complete way to enumerate a placed footprint's geometry — e.g. component.Children.OfType<PcbComponentBody>() for its 3D bodies, or CoordRect.Union(component.Children.Select(c => c.Bounds)) for its true extent. Re-evaluated on each enumeration, so it always reflects the current document. Each primitive appears once, even when it is present in both the child collection and the document's flat list (component pads).

member.summary: Moves the whole footprint by the given offset: shifts the component reference point (/) and every primitive in — pads, tracks, vias, arcs, text, fills, courtyard regions and 3D bodies — so the footprint stays internally consistent. Net and component assignments are preserved.
member.param: The X offset.
The Y offset.

member.summary: Moves the whole footprint so its reference point (/) sits at , shifting every owned primitive by the same offset. See .

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbComponent.RotateBy(System.Double,System.Nullable{OriginalCircuit.Eda.Primitives.CoordPoint})
member.summary: Rotates the whole footprint counter-clockwise by about (the component reference point / by default): turns every primitive in — positions and per-primitive orientation (pad/text/fill spin, arc angles, 3D-model 2D/Z rotation) — and updates , so the geometry and the metadata stay consistent. Net and component assignments are preserved.
member.param: The rotation angle in degrees (counter-clockwise).
The pivot to rotate about; defaults to the component reference point.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbDocument.BoardParametersOrdered
member.summary: Board-level parameters as an ordered key/value list — the canonical, authorable representation of the Board6 record. It preserves key order and the duplicate keys that (a flat dictionary convenience view) collapses: the block concatenates a main board-parameter section, a board-region sub-block, and repeated RECORD=-delimited layer-stack/split-plane sub-records, so several keys (the common SELECTION..UNIONINDEX prefix, SPLITLINECOUNT, RECORD) appear more than once. When non-null this list is written verbatim (byte-faithful round-trip); set it to author a Board6 with exact ordering/duplicates. When null, the writer falls back to .

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbDocument.FileGuid
member.summary: Per-document GUID from the modern FileHeaderSix stream. Round-tripped from a loaded document; a freshly created document defaults to a new GUID so it is authored with the identity Altium expects. Set to null only when a loaded document had no FileHeaderSix stream (so the writer reproduces its absence exactly).

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbDocument.LayerStack
member.summary: Layer stack parsed from Board6 parameters. Lazily computed on first access. Returns null if no layer data is present.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbDocument.GetStackup
member.summary: The physical board stack-up — an ordered (top-to-bottom) list of copper, dielectric, solder-mask and silkscreen layers with true millimetre thicknesses and absolute Z positions — parsed from the modern V9_STACK_LAYER Board6 parameters. Lazily computed; returns when the file carries no usable stack data (callers can fall back to ). Unlike , this models the dielectric cores and exposes per-layer thickness, which is what 3D rendering needs.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbDocument.AdditionalStreams
member.summary: Additional OLE storages/streams preserved for round-trip fidelity. Key format: "StorageName/StreamName" -> byte data.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbDocument.Models
member.summary:
Embedded 3D STEP models referenced by component bodies (via ), modeled from the root Models storage (Models/Data metadata + numbered Models/<n> zlib STEP payloads). Mirrors .
Populated by the reader and reconstructed by the writer, so models added here are written to the file. The metadata round-trips byte-for-byte; the numbered STEP streams round-trip their decoded content (the zlib bytes themselves may differ, the accepted library-wide limitation). Empty when the document carries no embedded models.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbDocument.ModelsStoragePresent
member.summary: True when the source file carried a Models storage (so the writer reproduces it even when empty). Set by the reader.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbDocument.GetFramingBounds
member.summary: The world-space rectangle a renderer should frame the whole board to when auto-zooming. Unlike (which measures only placed/free primitives and components), this also folds in the physical board outline from , so the board edge — which usually extends past the outermost copper (edge clearance, mounting margins, tabs) — is fully visible rather than cropped.
member.remarks:
Falls back to when the document has no Board6 outline, so boards built from primitives alone still frame correctly. When an outline is present the result is always non-degenerate, which also fixes the outline-only board that would otherwise render tiny ( makes CoordTransform.AutoZoom early-return).
Primitives lying entirely outside the board outline — off-board notes, title blocks and (auto-placed) hidden component designators/comments — are excluded, so a board that carries such off-sheet clutter still frames tightly to the physical board instead of zooming far out. Content that touches the board (the usual edge overhang: clearance, tabs, mounting margins) is kept, since its bounding box still intersects the outline's.

member.name: F:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbLayerStack.AlwaysEnabledLayers
member.summary: Parses a layer stack from Board6 (or PcbLib Library/Data header) parameters. The layer index N is the same numeric PCB layer ID used everywhere else (1=Top Layer, 32=Bottom Layer, 57-72=Mechanical 1-16, etc.) — a footprint's LAYER69NAME entry, say, names whatever the document/library author renamed layer 69 to (e.g. "Top Assembly" or "Top Courtyard"), which need not match the generic "Mechanical N" default, so callers should always resolve names through this per-file table rather than assuming the defaults. Returns null if no layer stack data is present.

member.summary: The layer-id → layer-kind mapping table (PcbDoc only; empty in PcbLib). Each entry maps a physical layer id to a layer-kind enum value. Fully typed so the table round-trips and is authored from scratch without replaying the raw bytes.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbLayerKindMapping.Signature
member.summary: A 32-bit content checksum Altium writes immediately before the mapping table (0 when the table is empty). It is — MurmurHash2-32 over the packed entry buffer. On round-trip the value read from disk is preserved verbatim (some Altium-saved files hash a couple of bytes of uninitialised heap past the buffer, so their stored value is not exactly reproducible); for a from-scratch table the writer fills it in via . Altium does not validate this field on load, so a computed value is always accepted.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbLayerKindMapping.ComputeSignature
member.summary: Computes the layer-kind-mapping signature exactly as Altium's TLayerKindMappingSection does: MurmurHash2-32 (seed 0xDEADBEEF, multiplier 0x5BD1E995) over a packed buffer of 5 bytes per entry (int32 little-endian followed by the low byte of ), consumed as ceil(n/4) 32-bit little-endian words with the final partial word zero-filled (Altium uses no MurmurHash2 tail step). Returns 0 for an empty table.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbModel.ComputeChecksum(System.ReadOnlySpan{System.Byte})
member.summary: Parses a PCB "Models" storage into instances. Model metadata comes from the Data stream (a sequence of length-prefixed, pipe-delimited parameter records, one per model: ID, NAME, EMBED, MODELSOURCE, ROTX/Y/Z, DZ, CHECKSUM); each model's STEP payload comes from the matching numbered stream (0, 1, ...), zlib-compressed. Shared by the PcbLib reader (Library/Models) and the PcbDoc model view (root Models storage).

Computes the Altium 3D-model checksum: a position-weighted byte sum over the uncompressed STEP payload, mod 2^32. The weight of byte i is 1 for i==0 and i otherwise. (Reverse-engineered; e.g. the payload [10,20,30,40,50] yields 410.) Use this when authoring a model from scratch; loaded models preserve their stored .

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbModel.RecomputeChecksum
member.summary: Recomputes from the current (UTF-8 encoded). Call after setting on a model authored from scratch.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbNamedParameterStorage
member.summary:
A named PcbDoc parameter-block storage that holds editor/DRC settings or violation records — e.g. Design Rule Checker Options6, Advanced Placer Options6, Pin Swap Options6, SimbeorCacheSection, TMatchedNetLengthsViolation, CustomShapes, WaivedViolations, PinPairsSection. Each is a Header + Data storage whose Data is a sequence of length-prefixed |KEY=VALUE| blocks (the same framing as Nets6).
Modeled as typed parameter records instead of an opaque AdditionalStreams blob so the data is fully readable and reproducible from scratch. The storage Header is captured verbatim because its meaning varies by storage (a record count for some, a modified/dirty flag for others) and is not derivable.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbPad.Sr5Length
member.summary: Length of SubRecord 5 (the main pad block) as read from the source. PcbLib pads use 202 bytes; PcbDoc pads use 194. Captured so the writer reproduces the original length rather than always emitting 202. Defaults to 202 for pads created from scratch.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbPad.PadSubrecord2
member.summary: SubRecord 2 (a Pascal string, usually empty) captured from the source so non-default values round-trip. Null for pads built from scratch (written as an empty string).

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbPad.FullStackEntries
member.summary: Per-layer full-stack opening entries appended after the 596-byte size/shape block for full-stack pads (e.g. rounded-rectangle SMD pads). Each entry carries a layer code, flags, X/Y size and corner percentage. Empty for simple pads.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbPad.IdentityGuid
member.summary: Per-pad unique identity GUID (SubRecord-5 offsets 126-141, "GUID-A"). Round-tripped from a loaded pad; freshly generated per pad when authored from scratch (Altium does not enforce uniqueness — duplicates load fine — but distinct ids match how Altium authors new primitives).

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbPad.IdentityGuidB
member.summary: Pad-stack / footprint-scoped identity GUID (SubRecord-5 offsets 142-157, "GUID-B"). Shared by all pads of one footprint and distinct per footprint; round-tripped from a loaded pad, generated once per component when authored from scratch.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbPad.SolderMaskCache
member.summary: SubRecord-5 solder-mask cache word (offsets 121-124). Usually mirrors the manual but is 0 for some pads, so it is modeled (round-tripped) rather than derived. Altium revalidates it on load.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbPad.ReservedMarker185
member.summary: SubRecord-5 reserved marker byte at offset 185 (observed values 0x03/0x01/0x11; default 0x03). Modeled so a loaded pad round-trips exactly; Altium does not require a specific value here.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbPad.MainBlockBaseShapes
member.summary: The main-block base shapes (ShapeTop/Middle/Bottom) modeled separately from the typed etc., which the reader overrides with the per-layer shape for rendering when overrides are active ( set). Altium keeps a base shape in the main block while the real per-layer shape lives in ; these preserve the base shapes for a byte-faithful round-trip. Null when the typed shapes are the base.

member.summary:
A shape-based region (ShapeBasedRegions6 storage). Like a region but with arc-capable extended outline vertices. Modeled byte-exact by preserving the raw header/length bytes and the typed geometry. See docs/decompile/feature-shapebased-regions.md.

member.summary: Moves this shape-based region/body by the given offset, shifting every outline and hole vertex (arc centers included) and the linked 3D-model placement (the MODEL.2D.X/MODEL.2D.Y properties, when present) so the 2D shape and the 3D model stay aligned.

The Y offset.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbShapeBasedRegion.Rotate(System.Double,OriginalCircuit.Eda.Primitives.CoordPoint)
member.summary: Rotates this shape-based region/body counter-clockwise by about : turns every outline and hole vertex (arc centres included) and the linked 3D-model placement — the MODEL.2D.X/MODEL.2D.Y point is rotated and the MODEL.2D.ROTATION placement angle is spun (when present). The intrinsic model mounting (MODEL.3D.ROTX/Y/Z) is left untouched — the renderer's in-plane rotation is MODEL.3D.ROTZ + MODEL.2D.ROTATION, so advancing both would rotate the body twice.
member.param: The rotation angle in degrees (counter-clockwise).
The point to rotate about.

member.summary: The three built-in (vector) stroke fonts that Altium ships in the default font table. These are the well-known low font-table IDs stored in a PCB text record's font field (see ); the underlying value is a font-table index, so values outside this set are possible (custom / TrueType fonts) and are represented directly by . member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbText.InvertedRectJustification
member.summary: Justification / anchor point of this text relative to — despite the name (kept for compatibility with the byte's original, narrower assumed purpose), this applies to EVERY text object, not just ones with set. is the text's bottom-left corner only when this is (or /unset); any other value means Location is some other point in the text's own box (e.g. means Location IS the center, so the rendered text grows symmetrically outward from it regardless of string length — important for a special string like ".Designator" that gets substituted with a variable-length value later). Confirmed against a user-supplied test library: two text objects with identical Height/font but different Justification (5=CenterCenter, 3=LeftBottom) stored different Location values for the same intended visual position, with the delta matching the glyph block's own measured half-width/half-height. Uses the Altium PCB encoding (), which differs from the schematic TextJustification ordering. Read/written unconditionally at offset 132 (see PcbLibReader.ReadText / PcbLibWriter), not gated behind .

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbText.BaseFontType
member.summary: Override for the SubRecord-1 base font-type byte (offset 43). The writer normally derives this from /; this captures the exact byte only when the source disagrees with the derived value (barcodes can carry a base font that the model flattens). Null otherwise (derive). Keeps round-trip byte-exact without breaking from-scratch authoring.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbText.TextKindByte
member.summary: Override for the SubRecord-1 authoritative text-kind byte (offset 160). Normally derived from ; captures the exact byte only when the source disagrees. Null otherwise.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbText.FontFieldRaw
member.summary: Exact 64-byte primary font-name field (offsets 46-109), captured only when its bytes after the name's null terminator are non-zero. That trailing "dirt" is non-deterministic stale heap memory Altium leaves from a reused buffer — observed to contain leftover previous font names (e.g. "…New Roman"), heap pointers, even fragments of another record's parameter block — so it is irreducible: it cannot be reconstructed from the model. It affects ~half of real-world texts. Null when the field is clean, in which case the writer emits the modeled zero-padded (deterministic). From-scratch texts always write clean; this capture only lets a loaded file round-trip byte-for-byte.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbText.BarCodeFontFieldRaw
member.summary: Exact 64-byte barcode font-name field (offsets 161-224), captured only when its trailing padding is non-zero (same irreducible stale-heap dirt as ). Null otherwise (writer emits the modeled zero-padded).

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PcbSmartUnion
member.summary: A PcbDoc SmartUnions record: a union grouping of board objects (via-stitching arrays, trace-tuning patterns, polygon-pour unions, etc.). On disk each record concatenates several member sub-blocks into one length-prefixed parameter block; every member begins with the common primitive prefix (SELECTION..UNIONINDEX), so that prefix marks the member boundaries. The record is fully typed and authorable — populate , each carrying its typed prefix plus the member-specific keys (in source order) as . The member-specific keys vary enormously by union type (via geometry, indexed ACCLIST{n} stitching/vertex arrays, trace-tuning keys), so they are kept as an ordered key/value list rather than hundreds of named fields; this is the natural model and round-trips byte-for-byte.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PlaneConnectStyle
member.summary: How a pad or via connects to an internal power/ground plane. Mirrors Altium's TPlaneConnectStyle (eReliefConnectToPlane, eDirectConnectToPlane, eNoConnect) and is the stored value behind the pad/via "Plane Connection" setting shown in the Altium properties panel.

remarks.para: The underlying byte is verified against Altium's own scripting API: in PCBObjectInspector.pas the value of IPCB_Pad2.PowerPlaneConnectStyle indexes the array ['eReliefConnectToPlane', 'eDirectConnectToPlane', 'eNoConnect'], so 0 is a thermal-relief connection, 1 is a solid/direct connection and 2 is no connection. The thermal-relief geometry (conductor width, entries, air gap and expansion) only applies when the style is .

This is the pad/via's stored/configured style — the value shown in the footprint pad properties and the one the relief geometry belongs to. It is not necessarily the context-dependent effective style that Altium's scripting API computes for a placed board: in a footprint library (no power planes) the API reports every primitive as eNoConnect regardless of this stored value.

member.name: F:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PlaneConnectStyle.Direct
member.summary: Solid/direct connection. Altium eDirectConnectToPlane.

member.name: F:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Pcb.PlaneConnectStyle.NoConnect
member.summary: No connection to the plane. Altium eNoConnect.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Project.AltiumProject
member.summary: An Altium PCB project (.PrjPcb): the list of documents that make up a board design together with its configurations, variants, parameters and output jobs, and (when available) the compiled logical sheet hierarchy from the sibling .PrjPcbStructure file.

remarks.para: The project file is a flat INI-style text document. is the raw, ordered representation that the writer emits verbatim, which is what makes a project round-trip byte-for-byte. The typed collections (, , , …) are lightweight views computed over those sections, so reading them is always consistent with and editing through a view writes straight back.
Use to load a project, then the Open…Async helpers here to open its individual documents with the existing readers.

member.summary: Document header parameters from the FileHeader record (RECORD=31 equivalent). Contains page size, font definitions, grid settings, and other document metadata. When null, defaults (HEADER + WEIGHT) are written for new files.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchDocument.SheetSettings
member.summary: Sheet settings record (RECORD=31) containing font definitions, grid/border/title-block settings. Preserved as raw parameters for round-trip fidelity.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchDocument.AdditionalStreams
member.summary: Additional OLE storages/streams preserved for round-trip fidelity. Key format: "StreamName" for root streams, "StorageName/StreamName" for nested streams.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchDocument.OpaqueRecords
member.summary: Opaque (unmodeled) records preserved for round-trip fidelity. Each entry is the raw parameter dictionary from an unrecognized record type.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchDocument.HeaderParametersOrdered
member.summary: The FileHeader document-header block as an ordered, authorable key/value list — the canonical representation, preserving key order and any duplicate keys the dictionary collapses. Emitted verbatim when set; the typed model / remain the from-scratch authoring surface.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchDocument.ReadOrderedRecords
member.summary: Every FileHeader record (after the document header) captured in original record order, each linked to its typed model object (the primitive/component it produced, or a holder for sheet/marker/opaque records). The writer walks this list to reproduce the exact on-disk order, emitting each record's captured ordered parameters so unmodeled parameters round-trip exactly. This replaces the former detached whole-document record blob: the captured parameters now live with the model object, matching the PCB and SchLib pattern. Null (or after binary-pin records) falls back to typed-model serialization that supports from-scratch authoring. This is the authorable, byte-faithful representation of the document's record stream.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchDocument.LoadedPrimitiveCount
member.summary: Count of modeled top-level primitives captured immediately after the document was read. The writer compares it against the live count to decide whether the byte-faithful fast path is still valid: if a primitive was added or removed after load the counts differ and the writer falls back to typed serialization so the edit is not dropped. Null for documents built from scratch.

member.summary: Font table parsed from the sheet settings (RECORD=31) FontID table, used for rendering text.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchDocument.SystemFont
member.summary: The document's system (default) font — a 1-based index into . Objects that don't carry their own FontId (pins, sheet entries) render with this font, not the first entry. From the SystemFont sheet-settings value; defaults to 1.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchOpaqueRecord
member.summary: A schematic record whose type is not modelled by the library. Its raw parameter block is captured on read so it can be re-emitted verbatim at its original position, letting unsupported records (e.g. notes, hyperlinks, harness constructs in a SchLib) round-trip instead of being lost.

member.summary: The parsed parameters of the unmodelled record.

member.summary: The record's parameters as an ordered key/value list (preserving key order and any duplicates the dictionary collapses). Emitted verbatim when present so an unmodelled record round-trips byte-for-byte; null falls back to .

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchOrderedRecord
member.summary: One FileHeader record captured on read, linking the typed model object it produced to its original ordered parameters. The SchDoc writer walks to reproduce the exact on-disk record order; this is the document-level analogue of the SchLib per-component ReadOrderedPrimitives + RawRecordParams pairing, and of each PCB model's RawParametersOrdered. This is the authorable, byte-faithful representation of the document's record stream; the typed model collections remain the convenience/from-scratch authoring surface.

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchOrderedRecord.Model
member.summary: The typed model object this record produced — a primitive, a , or a holder for records with no first-class model (the RECORD=31 sheet settings, the implementation/map-definer container markers, and unknown record types).

member.name: P:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchOrderedRecord.OrderedParams
member.summary: The record's parameters in original key order (preserves duplicates and unmodeled keys).

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Models.Sch.SchRawRecord
member.summary: A holder for a captured SchDoc record that has no first-class typed model (RECORD=31 sheet settings, the implementation/map-definer container markers RECORD=44/46/48, and unrecognized record types). Keeps the record addressable in so the on-disk order and bytes round-trip without a detached parallel record list.

member.summary: Graphical primitives that belong to this sheet template — the border lines, title-block text and logo images drawn by the applied .SchDot. Altium stores them as records whose OWNERINDEX points at this template record (type 39). They are kept here, separate from the document's own top-level primitives, so they are not rendered or netlisted as regular schematic content (which would double-draw the sheet frame/title block) while still round-tripping on write.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Serialization.AltiumEncoding.DecodeUtf8ParameterValue(System.String)
member.summary: Decodes a parameter value that carried the %UTF8% key prefix. The surrounding parameter block is decoded as Windows-1252, so a UTF-8 value arrives as one char per raw byte ("mojibake"). Re-encoding those chars back to Windows-1252 bytes recovers the original UTF-8 byte sequence (the mapping is a byte bijection), which is then decoded as UTF-8.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Serialization.AltiumEncoding.EncodeUtf8ParameterValue(System.String)
member.summary: Inverse of : maps a Unicode string to the one-char-per-UTF-8-byte form so that, when the parameter block is subsequently encoded as Windows-1252, the value is emitted as its UTF-8 byte sequence (matching how Altium stores %UTF8%-prefixed parameters).

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Serialization.Compound.CompoundFileAccessor
member.summary: Provides async-friendly access to COM Structured Storage (compound) files.
member.remarks:
This is a thin wrapper around OpenMcdf 3.x. It fully encapsulates the OpenMcdf API surface (///) behind the library-neutral / types so readers and writers never reference OpenMcdf directly.
OpenMcdf 3.x replaced the 2.x CompoundFile/CFStorage/CFStream model with a root-storage that streams directly to its backing store. For reads we open the source stream (which now hardens against the cyclic directory-entry DoS the 2.3.0 advisories described). For writes we build in an in-memory root storage and copy the finished image out in , preserving the previous "build, then Save(stream)" usage shape.

member.name: T:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Serialization.Compound.CompoundStream
member.summary: Library-neutral handle to a single stream inside a compound (OLE structured storage) file.
member.remarks:
This deliberately hides the underlying OpenMcdf from the rest of the library. It is a lightweight handle bound to an owning and an entry name; it does NOT keep a stream open. Every / call opens (or creates) the backing stream and disposes it before returning.
This atomic open-read-dispose / create-write-dispose pattern is required by OpenMcdf 3.x: with a non-transacted root storage, only one may be in flight at a time and it must be disposed before the next entry is created or opened, otherwise its content is silently dropped. Keeping streams un-held makes the reader/writer call sites immune to that hazard.

member.summary: Encodes boolean properties into the flags word. All bits are computed from properties.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Serialization.Writers.PcbLibWriter.V7LayerId(System.Int32)
member.summary: Derives the "v7 saved layer id" (uint32) from the Altium layer number. This redundant field is written into primitive tails and must match the primitive's layer. Encoding (verified against the corpus and altium_monkey's PcbV7LayerPartition): 0x0100_0000+layer (signal 1-32), 0x0101_0000+(layer-38) (internal plane 39-54), 0x0102_0000+(layer-56) (mechanical 57-72), 0x0103_0000+partition (special layers). Mechanical layers past 16 (id 1000+N, N=layer-1000 — see PcbLibReader.MechanicalLayerId) extend the same 0x0102_0000 mechanical base with the absolute N, e.g. 0x0102_0000+20 for Mechanical 20; confirmed against this reader's own extraction of the equivalent field from real Altium output and cross-checked live in Altium up to Mechanical 89.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Serialization.Writers.PcbLibWriter.LegacyLayerByte(System.Int32)
member.summary: The legacy single-byte layer field written at primitive offset 0. For mechanical layers past 16 (id 1000+N) this is inherently lossy — Altium itself clamps it to Mechanical 16 (72) for backward compatibility with readers that predate the extended range, with the true layer recoverable only from (Region/ComponentBody) or the hidden secondary byte (Track/Text/...; see PcbLibReader.ResolveMechanicalLayerByte). Casting straight to byte without this clamp would silently wrap (e.g. layer 1020 -> byte 252), corrupting the file.

member.name: M:OriginalCircuit.Altium.Serialization.Writers.WriterUtilities.SanitizeSectionKey(System.String)
member.summary: Replaces every character OpenMcdf's writer rejects ('\', '/', ':', '!') with '_'. Applied both to freshly-generated keys (see ) and to section keys preserved from a prior read (PcbLibrary.SectionKeys/SchLibrary.SectionKeys) -- those can legitimately contain them too (real Altium-authored files sometimes do; OpenMcdf's own restriction is stricter than the actual format), and there is no way to re-create an entry with the exact original name in that case either, so the key must be re-mangled the same way on every write regardless of where it came from.
